name: Fujimorism
summary: Fujimorism is the political current of Alberto Fujimori's presidency of Peru (1990-2000) and the Fuerza Popular movement that carries his name. It combines a hard-line, order-first presidency that dissolved Congress in the 1992 self-coup and ruled through a strong executive, with a free-market programme of austerity, privatisation and trade opening, anti-insurgent security policy and outreach to the poor through direct appeals rather than parties.
scope: The government of Alberto Fujimori (1990-2000) and the 1993 constitution adopted under it, as the scholarship on 'el fujimorismo' (García Montero, Díaz-Terán) and Britannica describe them. The party platforms of Fuerza Popular under Keiko Fujimori and Kenji Fujimori's breakaway faction are not the basis of any answer.
